title: A broadcast run performs ZERO on-chain verification of its own outcome: Phase 7 executes in forge's local pass, and the compensating human check is unticked
description: `run()` calls `_phase7_wiringAssertions()` after `vm.stopBroadcast()`. Under `--broadcast --skip-simulation --slow`, forge executes the entire Solidity body ONCE in a local pass, collecting calldata; the resulting ~60 transactions are then signed on the Ledger and dispatched afterwards. Phase 7 therefore runs against the LOCAL EVM copy of the chain, before a single transaction has been sent, and asserts only that the PLAN is internally consistent. It cannot and does not observe post-broadcast mainnet state. The same is true of every in-phase post-condition (BPT conservation `:892-895`, `newBM` balance unchanged `:728-731`, `old.paused()` `:1134`, `V1 totalStaked == 0` `:1394`) and of Phase 8, which never runs under broadcast at all. The `//promotion-ready:dry` annotation presents 'Phase 7's full bidirectional wiring read-back' as a verification gate, which is accurate for the dry run and misleading for the broadcast. The only genuine on-chain confirmation the story defines is checklist line 1195, a '(Post-broadcast, HUMAN step)' item that is currently UNTICKED.
impact: A one-shot, multi-hour, 60+-transaction Ledger cutover over live funds (16,338 BPT, ~349 USDC, 781 phUSD of staker budget, five dispatcher indices) can complete with `forge` exiting 0 while a tx reverted on-chain due to state drift, or while a step landed differently than simulated, and nothing in the tooling detects it. `--skip-simulation` removes even the per-transaction pre-send sanity check. The system is left half-configured with mints reverting `OnlyDispatcher` on the affected index and no automated signal.
evidence: side-effects.json -> executed (preview exit 0), postconditionResults. Verified on fork at block 25659373: Phase 7 passed entirely, but the run was PREVIEW - the identical code path under --broadcast would evaluate the same assertions against pre-broadcast local state.
recommendation: Add a read-only verification entry point (e.g. `promotion-ready:verify`) that re-runs `_phase7_wiringAssertions()` as a standalone `forge script --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET` invocation against live post-broadcast state, and append it to the `:broadcast` and `:resume` npm chains after the patch script (`&& forge script ...:VerifyPromotionReady`). Phase 7 is already `internal view` and self-contained apart from the deployment addresses, which the progress file supplies - the refactor is mechanical. Until then, tick checklist line 1195 as a hard gate, not an optional sweep.

title: The progress file is stamped `deploymentStatus: "completed"` during the local pass, making the patch script's own gate structurally inert
description: `_writeProgressFileWithStatus("completed")` is called at the end of `run()` - i.e. at the end of forge's LOCAL execution pass, before any transaction is broadcast. `_trackDeployment`/`_trackConfig` write `"in_progress"` on every step during the same pass. Consequently `"in_progress"` is only ever observable after a LOCAL-pass revert (which also produces a non-zero forge exit), and any run that reaches the broadcast stage at all has already written `"completed"` with every step marked done. `patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js:122-124` gates on exactly `deploymentStatus === 'completed'`. The header at `:16-22` calls this gate 'necessary but not sufficient'; it is in fact necessary and unconditionally true at every point the patcher can run, i.e. it carries no information. The real protection is the `&&` short-circuit plus a manual hand-trim, both of which are correctly implemented and documented.
impact: An operator reading the patcher's header may believe `deploymentStatus` is an independent safety interlock against patching from a partial broadcast. It is not. If the patcher is ever invoked manually (outside the `&&` chain) after a crashed broadcast - a plausible recovery action - it will patch `mainnet-addresses.ts` with addresses for contracts that may never have been deployed, with no complaint. No on-chain funds are at risk; the blast radius is a wrong address file feeding the UI and downstream scripts.
evidence: script:402-404 (`if (!isPreview) _writeProgressFileWithStatus("completed")` inside run(), after Phase 7 and before the process exits); script:1957/1965 (`in_progress` on every track call); patcher:122-124. Fork run confirmed no progress file is written in preview mode at all.
recommendation: Either (a) write `"completed"` from the JS side after `forge script` returns 0 - i.e. have `patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js` itself accept an explicit `--confirm-broadcast` flag and stop reading `deploymentStatus` as evidence - or (b) restate the header honestly: 'deploymentStatus is written pre-broadcast and is NOT evidence that anything landed; the only interlocks are the `&&` short-circuit and the mandatory hand-trim against run-latest.json receipts.' Option (b) is a one-line documentation fix and is sufficient.

title: Kendu is whitelisted unconditionally while its BLOCKING fee-on-transfer probe is PREVIEW-only, and a taxed token bricks batchMint for every reward token
description: `bm_.setNudgeTokenWhitelist(KENDU, true)` at `:640-644` is unconditional. `_probeKenduFeeOnTransfer()` - which the story designates BLOCKING (checklist line 1154) - lives in `_phase8_previewSmokeTests()`, and Phase 8 runs only when `PREVIEW_MODE=true` (`run():402-408`). A `--broadcast` run therefore whitelists Kendu with the blocking gate never executing. The script is honest about this at `:636-639` and the story's post-review correction #2 documents it, so this is a disclosed design choice rather than a hidden one - but it is disclosed only in prose, and the enforcement is entirely on the operator remembering to run `promotion-ready:dry` first. The downstream consequence is disproportionate: `batchMint` step 3.5 loops `pullPendingStream` over the whole whitelist with NO try/catch (`BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:528-536`), so one confiscatory or reverting reward token bricks `batchMint` for USDC and phUSD too.
impact: Availability of the entire batch-mint reward path, contingent on a procedural step. For Kendu specifically the risk is currently nil and empirically closed: the fork probe returned exact 1e24-in/1e24-credited, and Kendu's ownership is renounced (`owner() == 0x0`) so its fee switches can never be moved again. The finding is that the STRUCTURE permits a future third reward token to be whitelisted on a broadcast run with no tax check at all. Recovery exists (`setNudgeTokenWhitelist(token,false)` is owner-only and immediate), so this is availability-with-a-lever, not loss.
evidence: side-effects.json -> phase8Results.kenduFeeOnTransferBLOCKING (PASS, exact, actuallyExercised: true, but PREVIEW-only). script:636-639 states the procedural nature explicitly; script:402-408 gates Phase 8.
recommendation: Make the gate structural rather than procedural: perform the round-trip probe INSIDE Phase 2, immediately before `setNudgeTokenWhitelist(KENDU, true)`, in BOTH modes. It needs no cheatcode when broadcasting - the owner can fund the probe from its own Kendu balance with a small amount, or the check can be reduced to a broadcast-safe static assertion (`buyTotalFees() == 0 && sellTotalFees() == 0 && owner() == address(0)`) that the script `require`s unconditionally. If the probe must stay preview-only, gate the whitelist call on a `KENDU_PREFLIGHT_PASSED=true` env var that only the dry run instructs the operator to set.

title: A user who stakes between snapshot generation and the on-chain pause is silently stranded on a paused, defunded, Pauser-deregistered V1 staker
description: Phase 6 step 7 migrates a user list frozen twice over: once when `snapshot-depletion-stakers.js` runs, and again when forge's local pass reads it. `NFTStakerDepletion.stake` is UNGATED during `Migrating` (`:550`, audit-20 M-05) and V1 is not paused until the `st_<label>_pause` transaction actually lands on-chain, potentially hours into the Ledger session. Any address staking in that window is absent from `users`, so `migrate(users)` skips it. The guard `require(old.totalStaked() == 0, "V1 still holds stake after migrate - widen the snapshot and re-run")` at `:1394` cannot catch it, because that require - like all of Phase 6 - evaluates during the local pass against the pre-broadcast snapshot of state (see PR-09). The affected user is then left on a V1 that is paused, unregistered from the global Pauser (so a later `Pauser.unpause()` will not reach it), and whose reward budget has been swept down to a ~1% residual by step 9.
impact: One or more users' staked NFT positions and future emissions are frozen on a defunct contract with no automatic recovery and no automatic detection. Funds are not lost - the owner can `setPauser`/`unpause`, re-run `migrate` (it is re-runnable by design) and re-fund V1 or top up V2 - but the user experiences a total loss of availability until a human notices. Probability is low today (6 stakers total across the three contracts, 2/146/13 units) but is a direct function of how long the snapshot is stale. The prerequisite script's own header (`snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:37-40`) anticipates the case and calls it 'at worst left on V1', which understates the post-sweep, post-deregistration end state.
evidence: side-effects.json -> prerequisite (snapshot proven complete at block 25659373: 1/2/3 users, sums 2/146/13 == totalStaked). script:1388-1398; NFTStakerDepletion.sol:550 vs NFTStakerDepletionV2.sol:557; Phase 6 step 5 pause ordering at script:1371-1378.
recommendation: Close the window rather than narrow it: split the pause out of the frozen plan. Either (a) pause all three V1 stakers in a separate, short broadcast BEFORE generating the snapshot, so the user list is taken against an already-frozen contract - the snapshot header's 'does NOT need to be taken after a pause' rationale then no longer applies and the list becomes provably final; or (b) add a hard freshness gate: record the snapshot's `blockNumber` in the JSON (it already is) and `require(snapshotBlock >= block.number - N)` in Phase 0 so a stale list cannot be consumed at all. (b) is cheap and also fixes PR-03's late-failure problem. Independently, keep the story's 'Open items carried to review' instruction - re-run `promotion-ready:snapshot` immediately before the session - as an operator gate.

title: Phase 4d's post-pause residue sweep can never fire, so its stated rationale and the story's 'rescueERC20 still works while paused' assertion are both unproven
description: Autonomous Decision 2 states: 'Donors keep pushing USDC at the old sink for the whole interval between Phase 3's rescue and their own repoint... On the dry run the residue was 0 (Phase 3 ran seconds earlier); on a real multi-hour Ledger session it will not be.' That reasoning does not survive forge's execution model. `uint256 residue = IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER)` at `:1140` is evaluated in the LOCAL pass, seconds after Phase 3's local rescue - so `residue` is 0 there too, the `if (residue > 0)` branch is never taken, and NO rescue transaction is ever queued. Whatever USDC actually accumulates on the old minter during the multi-hour broadcast is not swept. The trailing `require(balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0)` at `:1148` likewise only evaluates locally and passes vacuously. Confirmed empirically on the fork: the run logged 'no residue to sweep'. As a second-order effect, the story's checklist line 1166 requires asserting 'that `rescueERC20` still works while paused' - the else branch at `:1146` merely LOGS that claim as prose; nothing proves it.
impact: A small, bounded amount of USDC (donations landing on the old sink between Phase 3 and each donor's repoint) is left on a paused, retired contract instead of entering the stream. It is fully recoverable at any later time - `rescueERC20` is `onlyOwner` and not pause-gated - so this is stranded-value-pending-a-manual-step, not loss. The more material defect is the false confidence: a documented Autonomous Decision claims a leak is closed when it is not, and a checklist item claims an assertion exists when the code only prints a sentence.
evidence: side-effects.json -> postconditionResults (last entry) and stateWrites (old BatchNFTMinter USDC 225040608 -> 0 via Phase 3 only). Fork log: '=== Phase 4d ... paused (batchMint now reverts EnforcedPause) / no residue to sweep (rescueERC20 remains available while paused)'.
recommendation: Two independent fixes. (1) Make the sweep unconditional so a rescue transaction is always queued: replace the `if (residue > 0)` branch with an unconditional `rescueERC20(USDC, OWNER, type(uint256).max)`-style full-balance call if the legacy minter supports it, or - since it does not - add an explicit post-broadcast operator step to the runbook and drop Autonomous Decision 2's claim that the leak is structurally closed. (2) Prove the pause-transparency property in Phase 8 instead: `deal` 1 USDC onto the paused old minter and assert `rescueERC20` succeeds, which is a real test rather than a comment.

title: Indices 2 and 3 are never functionally exercised, so `setMinter` on two of the three new Uniboosts has no verification of any kind - and Autonomous Decision 5 claims otherwise
description: Autonomous Decision 5 removes the `dispatcher.minter()` read-back from Phase 7 on the correct grounds that `ATokenDispatcherV2._minter` is `internal` with no accessor, and substitutes: 'Phase 8's mints verify it MORE strongly than a read-back would... a dispatcher whose minter was not set reverts on the first mint through its index, which all three donor-path probes exercise.' The same claim is repeated verbatim in the code at `:1575-1580`. But the three probes cover indices 1, 4 and 7 - `_mintOnce(IDX_EYE)`, `_mintOnce(IDX_RATCHET)`, and the inline pooler mint at `IDX_POOLER`. Indices 2 (Uniboost SCX) and 3 (Uniboost FLX) are never minted through. `newUniboostSCX.setMinter()` and `newUniboostFLX.setMinter()` therefore have neither a read-back (impossible) nor a functional probe (absent), and the story's checklist line 1174 asks for 'a donation on each of the four donor paths'.
impact: Low in practice: all three Uniboosts are configured by the same `_swapUniboost` body in one `ub_<label>_config` block, so a `setMinter` omission on SCX/FLX but not EYE is not a realistic failure. The real defect is that the claimed verification argument is false, which is precisely the comment-drift class this story's own checklist line 1161 ('every comment traceable to pinned source') exists to eliminate - and this drift survived the review that caught two others. If it were ever wrong, the symptom would be post-cutover mints on indices 2/3 reverting 'ATokenDispatcherV2: caller is not minter', discovered by a user rather than the runbook.
evidence: side-effects.json -> externalCalls (idx2 and idx3 both 'NEVER EXERCISED'). script:1670-1672 mints idx 1 and idx 7 only; script:1675-1698 mints idx 4. Fork log '--- donor paths ---' shows exactly three entries plus the structural SYA note.
recommendation: Add `_mintOnce(actor, IDX_SCX, USDC, "Uniboost SCX (idx 2)")` and `_mintOnce(actor, IDX_FLX, USDC, "Uniboost FLX (idx 3)")` to `_probeDonorPaths` - two lines, using the helper that already exists, closing the gap and making Autonomous Decision 5's argument true as written. Simultaneously correct the code comment at `:1575-1580` and the Autonomous Decision text to say 'all five donor-path probes' once they exist, or to name the covered indices explicitly if they are not added.

title: Phase 7's BPT conservation assertion degrades to `>= 0` on every resume path, leaving the largest asset in the cutover unverified exactly when verification matters most
description: `require(IERC20(BALANCER_POOL).balanceOf(newPooler) >= bptAtPhase0)` compares against `bptAtPhase0`, which is read fresh in Phase 0 at `:505` as `balanceOf(OLD_POOLER)`. On a `:resume` leg where the BPT move already landed on-chain, the old pooler holds 0, so `bptAtPhase0 == 0` and the assertion becomes `balanceOf(newPooler) >= 0` - unconditionally true, even if the 16,338 BPT were sitting on a third address. The companion assertion `require(balanceOf(OLD_POOLER) == 0)` at `:1563` still holds, but 'the old pooler is empty' and 'the new pooler is full' are different claims, and only the vacuous one covers the second. This is the one step the `//promotion-ready:resume` annotation itself singles out as 'THE ONE STEP A BAD RESUME COULD RUIN'.
impact: No direct loss path; the six `_moveBPT` guard rails were independently assessed as effective in every enumerated resume branch (a phantom pooler address fails `owner() == OWNER` and `code.length > 0`; an already-zero old balance ABORTS rather than re-running; an incorrectly-trimmed `pooler_bpt` flag is caught by the non-vacuous `balanceOf(OLD_POOLER) == 0`). The finding is that the resume path loses its positive confirmation that 16,338.8190 BPT is where it should be, precisely on the code path the runbook flags as highest-risk.
evidence: side-effects.json -> postconditionResults (Phase 7 BPT entry) and stateWrites (BPT old 16338818951239025717919 -> 0, new 0 -> 16338818951239025717919, exact conservation asserted both ways on the fresh path). Fork run exercised the fresh path only; the resume degradation is established by reading `bptAtPhase0`'s assignment at :505 against `_requireSlot`'s resume-aware semantics at :524-527.
recommendation: Persist the Phase 0 BPT reading across resumes rather than re-deriving it. Record it in the progress file as a first-class entry (the `ContractDeployment` struct already carries unused `uint256` fields, or add a sibling `bptAtCutover` key) and, when a progress file is present, assert `balanceOf(newPooler) >= recordedBpt` instead of the freshly-read zero. A cheaper stopgap: when `_isConfigured("pooler_bpt")` is true, assert `balanceOf(newPooler) > 0` at minimum, so the resume path is never fully vacuous.

title: The snapshot file is a documented hard prerequisite with no Phase 0 probe; it fails at line 1390 of 2171 with a generic filesystem error
description: `scripts/snapshots/depletion-stakers-latest.json` is named a hard prerequisite by the `//promotion-ready`, `//promotion-ready:dry` and `//promotion-ready:resume` annotations and by the script NatSpec at `:129-131`, and it is deliberately gitignored (Autonomous Decision 8). Yet Phase 0 - the designated `require`-gated precondition phase, which checks 17 owners, 5 dispatcher slots, 5 prime tokens, 6 donor sinks and 5 hooks - never probes for it. The first read is `vm.readFile(SNAPSHOT_FILE)` at `:1441`, untry'd, reached from `:1390` inside Phase 6, after roughly 50 transactions have already been built. The failure surfaces as Foundry's generic fs error, not as 'run promotion-ready:snapshot first'. Separately, `promotion-ready:snapshot` is the only one of the five npm keys with no `//` annotation.
impact: Fail-closed and atomic - because the whole body executes locally before any dispatch (true even under `--skip-simulation`), a missing snapshot aborts the run before a single transaction is broadcast, so nothing is half-applied on mainnet. The cost is operator time and an unactionable error message at the worst moment: mid-session on a resume, with a Ledger connected. Not a funds risk.
evidence: closure-manifest.json -> missingSnapshotAnalysis (verdict: FAIL CLOSED on all three cases). script:1440-1443 (no try/catch); script:417-522 (Phase 0 contains no snapshot check); package.json:283 (unannotated key).
recommendation: Add to Phase 0: `try vm.readFile(SNAPSHOT_FILE) returns (string memory j) { require(bytes(j).length > 0, "snapshot file empty - run: npm run promotion-ready:snapshot"); } catch { revert("snapshot missing - run: npm run promotion-ready:snapshot"); }`, and while there, parse `.blockNumber` and assert freshness (which also addresses PR-11). Add a `//promotion-ready:snapshot` annotation to package.json documenting the prerequisite relationship, the `FROM_BLOCK` horizon and exit code 4.

title: The snapshot scanner's `DEFAULT_FROM_BLOCK = 25000000` is an undocumented correctness horizon for the migrate() user list
description: `const DEFAULT_FROM_BLOCK = 25000000n` bounds the `Staked`/`Unstaked`/`DepositedFor` log scan that produces Phase 6's `migrate()` user list. Any position opened before block 25,000,000 yields a short list unless `FROM_BLOCK` is overridden. Neither the story, the script NatSpec, nor the (absent) npm annotation records that this constant is load-bearing for migration completeness. The script does carry two real guards - `die(4, ...)` when `totalStaked > 0` but zero holders were found (`:242-243`), and a `sumStaked != totalStaked` WARNING (`:245-248`) - but the WARNING is non-fatal and prints to stdout only, so a PARTIAL under-enumeration emits a snapshot the Foundry script then trusts.
impact: None today, and this was verified rather than assumed: the run at the pin block reconciled EXACTLY on all three stakers (1 user / sum 2 == totalStaked 2; 2 users / 146 == 146; 3 users / 13 == 13), so the horizon is currently sufficient and the emitted list is provably complete. The finding is latent: the guarantee rests on an undocumented magic number, and the partial-miss case degrades to a warning rather than a refusal.
evidence: side-effects.json -> prerequisite.perStaker (all three `match: true`) and prerequisite.residualRisk. Snapshot run output: 'Scanning blocks 25000000 .. 25659373'; per-staker 'holders with non-zero stake: N (sum=X, on-chain totalStaked=X)'.
recommendation: Promote the `sumStaked !== totalStaked` warning at `:245-248` to a hard `die(4, ...)`: a list that does not reconcile against `totalStaked` is exactly the subset case the header says to avoid, and `migrate` being re-runnable makes a false abort cheap while a silent subset is expensive. Additionally, document `DEFAULT_FROM_BLOCK` as 'must precede the earliest of the three stakers' deployment blocks' and record those three block numbers in the comment so the constant can be audited rather than trusted.

title: The Phase 6 budget top-up approval lacks the before/after allowance assertions that guard every other approval in the script
description: `IERC20(PHUSD).approve(v2, movable); NFTStakerDepletionV2(v2).topUp(movable);` at `:1409-1410` has no pre-check that the existing allowance is zero and no post-check that it returned to zero. The script's own USDC donation helper `_collectNudgeFromOwner` does both, and states the reason explicitly: 'The allowance is fully consumed inside `collectNudge`, so it always returns to 0 - asserted here so a stale approval can never silently accumulate' (`:742-744`, `:753`). Three separate `approve` calls run across the three stakers with no such guard. The story's own review flagged the adjacent `approve` vs `forceApprove` inconsistency as 'minor, non-blocking'; the missing assertions are a distinct and sharper omission.
impact: If `topUp` ever pulled less than `movable`, a residual phUSD allowance from the Ledger owner to a V2 staker contract would persist silently and unbounded in time. Concretely low: `topUp` is `onlyOwner` on a contract deployed moments earlier in the same script, and the fork run showed exact consumption (swept 4.6326 / 708.8243 / 51.9974 phUSD with V2 balances matching). This is defence-in-depth parity, not a live bug.
evidence: side-effects.json -> stateWrites (OWNER EOA phUSD allowance entry, 'no pre-check, no post-check, plain approve not forceApprove'), contrasted with the USDC allowance entry asserted 0 both sides. script:744/753 vs script:1409.
recommendation: Mirror the USDC helper exactly: `require(IERC20(PHUSD).allowance(OWNER, v2) == 0, "stale V2 topUp allowance");` before, `forceApprove` (or `approve`) in the middle, and `require(IERC20(PHUSD).allowance(OWNER, v2) == 0, "topUp left allowance behind");` after. Three lines per staker, and it makes the script's approval hygiene uniform - which is the actual value, since a reader currently cannot tell whether the asymmetry is deliberate.

title: The knowingly-accepted mint-UI breakage has no tracked remediation story, so the cutover ships an indefinite outage
description: Whitelisting three reward tokens makes `batchMint`'s `minRewards` array length-3, and `getNudgeTokens()` reorders on removal (swap-and-pop), so callers must re-fetch immediately before every call. The `//promotion-ready` annotation and the script both record that 'the live mint UI is BROKEN until a phlimbo-ui story ships a 3-element array plus a getNudgeTokens() re-fetch'. The story's own 'Open items carried to review' (line 1447) then states: 'The phlimbo-ui follow-up story ... is still unraised. The live mint UI breaks the moment this broadcasts. Tracked as a comment at story-dependencies.md:218.' A comment in a dependencies file is not a raised story. The acceptance is genuine and informed (Law 3: the owner knows), but the breakage is unbounded in duration rather than sequenced.
impact: User-facing mint availability via the UI is lost from the moment of broadcast until an unscheduled follow-up ships. No funds at risk; the contracts are correct and direct/multicall callers are unaffected. This is scheduling and disclosure, not a code defect - filed so it is visible rather than resolved inside a package.json comment.
evidence: package.json:282 ('KNOWN BREAKAGE, KNOWINGLY ACCEPTED'); story lines 376-377, 1194(a), 1447. Fork run corroborates the mechanism: `batchMint` with a 2-element array reverted `BatchMint__ArrayLengthMismatch(3, 2)` while the 3-element call succeeded.
recommendation: Raise the phlimbo-ui story before the Ledger session and sequence it as a same-day follow-up, so the outage window is a known number of hours rather than open-ended. If the cutover must go first, state the expected remediation date in the completion summary. Related: the two-coexisting-batch-minter-ABIs trap (legacy 3-arg on the four per-token minters, 4-arg multi-token on the shared one) belongs in that story's scope explicitly, since a UI that re-fetches `getNudgeTokens()` against a legacy minter will revert - that view does not exist there.

title: QA: the new StableYieldAccumulator is given an unbounded phlimbo approval that is hardcoded rather than mirrored from the retiring instance
description: Phase 5 mirrors the retiring accumulator's configuration field by field - `rewardToken`, `phlimbo`, `nftMinter`, `discountRate`, three `tokenConfigs`, three strategies, `nudgeSplit` - each read live off `OLD_SYA`. One value is not mirrored: `sya.approvePhlimbo(type(uint256).max)` is a hardcoded infinite approval. The inline comment justifies the mechanism ('collectReward pulls via transferFrom') but not the magnitude, and the project's own CLAUDE.md Configuration Safety section names caps and unbounded allowances as parameters requiring explicit justification rather than a default.
impact: Negligible in isolation - PhlimboV2 is a first-party contract and an infinite approval to it is the conventional pattern for a pull-based reward collector. Filed as QA because it is the single value in Phase 5 that breaks the 'read it off the live instance' discipline the rest of the phase follows, and because an unbounded allowance to a repointable dependency is worth a deliberate sentence rather than an implicit one.
evidence: side-effects.json -> stateWrites (approvePhlimbo entry). script:1185-1205 shows every neighbouring value sourced from `old.<getter>()`; only :1187 is a literal.
recommendation: Either read the retiring instance's existing phlimbo allowance and mirror it, or keep `type(uint256).max` and extend the comment to record why unbounded is correct here (PhlimboV2 is first-party, the approval is scoped to one spender, and `collectReward` is the only consumer) so the choice reads as deliberate rather than defaulted.
